title: UFV-01 (AC-13): this fork assertion has not run under the real fork project
severity_rationale: S2 by the plan: an unexecuted rail assertion can hide a fork-mode leak. Capital none: no fork test runs against live funds and the bot is off.

evidence.note: Assertion: fork project rails (SPEC R4) > module scope: the Telegram token and every test/.env.test key except the fork shell keys equal their sentinels (AC-13) Why not run: npm run test:fork starts Hardhat through the fork globalSetup (test/fork/setup.ts), and Phase 22 runs no Hardhat command (AC-08) Rehearsal: test/rails/vitest.fork-rehearsal.config.ts (project fork-rehearsal: the fork project's setupFiles, fileParallelism, pool and timeouts pinned by test/unit/rails/forkRehearsalParity.test.ts, without the Hardhat globalSetup) Result: pass (vpu-20261107T042012-23448-c57d66)

sibling_sites_checked: Each entry of unrun-fork-verifications.json has one obligation. Proven meanwhile by: test/unit/rails/childRails.test.ts setup-fork child cases (railsEntry 'setup-fork': sentinel env, fork mode, Telegram deny on, DB denied; fork shell keys (i)-(v))
escaped_regression: A fork worker that received a real Telegram token or app key under the real fork project (for example from a future change to the fork setup) would pass every rehearsal, because the rehearsal has no Hardhat globalSetup.
recommendation: Run it by name at the first npm run test:fork of v7.0, owner Phase 25 (ROADMAP Phase 25 success criterion 3) or any earlier phase that runs the fork suite, and record pass or fail for this named assertion.
